text:
maya: quick thought  we have fallback switches in the router but no standardized retention tiers. do we want a graded retention model (meta-only, short payload, forensic) tied to fallback reasons?
ron: yes. propose three tiers: metadata-only (ids/latencies), payload-trim (first/last n tokens), and forensic (full but redacted).
viv: +1. name-wise i like: 'summary', 'snapshot', 'forensic'. makes it easier in the Console.
leo: we should map tiers to triggers. e.g. snapshot on error-rate > 1% for 5m; forensic if elevated for 15m OR customer-requested escalation.
maya: sounds good. two UX constraints: 1) surface expected storage and cost delta on the rollout card; 2) always show who enabled forensic captures and why in the audit trail.
trace-bot: alert: fallback-rate for model:mistral-lite spiked 2.8x at 2024-06-12T03:11Z (baseline 0.6% -> 1.7%)
ron: ok linking triggers to policy DSL. draft sketch:
```
rollout {
  id: "r-2024-06-12-a"
  fallback {
    on_error_rate(rolling_5m > 0.01) -> retention: "snapshot";
    on_error_rate(rolling_15m > 0.015) -> retention: "forensic";
    on_manual_escalation(tag == "forensic-cs") -> retention: "forensic";
  }
}
```
viv: that DSL is great. also add a hard quota guard: retention_quota_bytes_per_org to prevent runaway costs.
amy: legal note: forensic tier must auto-redact PII patterns (emails, SSNs) before storing. mark access as restricted and require two-person approval for export.
leo: implementation note: router adds headers: X-Retention-Tier and X-Rollout-Evidence-Id. downstream ingestion uses those to route to different S3 prefixes with lifecycle rules.
maya: UI idea: rollout timeline should have a compact "evidence" column that shows retention tier changes, linked metric snapshots, and a one-click 'download evidence package' for restricted users.
ron: for observability, add a retention-meter on the model dashboard and a per-org retention budget widget (remaining bytes this billing cycle). color it amber when >70%.
viv: what about canaries? i think canary traffic should default to 'snapshot' for X minutes then fall back to 'summary' unless issue detected. saves us from over-retaining noisy early runs.
amy: agree but add explicit consent in workspaces with regulated data. some customers opt-in to full canary forensic for debug. this must be explicit.
leo: on API side, expose two endpoints: POST /v1/rollouts/:id/force-retention and GET /v1/rollouts/:id/evidence (with RBAC checks). also CLI flag `rw ctl rollout capture --tier forensic --reason \"CS request\"`
maya: auditing: every retention transition becomes an immutable event with actor, trigger-metric, sample-ids and signed evidence-id. important for compliance.
trace-bot: note: retention_quota for org:redwood-test set to 10GB/mo (used 6.2GB)
ron: ok action items:
- leo: prototype router header + prefix router (start staging)
- viv: console mockups: rollout timeline evidence column + retention-meter
- amy: redact rules + approval flow sketch for forensic exports
- maya: write draft policy DSL docs and customer opt-in wording
- ron: add quota enforcement hook in billing job
viv: i'll also add a small explainer blurb: \"Why we keep traces during fallback\" for the rollout card tooltip. short, non-technical.
maya: timeline: aim to have staging PRs for header + DSL parser by next Wednesday. if anyone sees privacy landmines ping amy earlier.
ron: will do. pinging the group in design standup tomorrow. :rocket:
